title: Private Deployment Watchtower: automated fix sagas for node degradation and upgrade safety
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, testable orchestration ("Watchtower") that detects common Private deployment degradations and runs safe, reversible remediation sagas driven by IaC primitives. This ticket scopes the runbook content, Terraform/SRE automation patterns, and the orchestration contracts for automated repairs and safe rolling upgrades.

Background: We continue to see transient node degradation and occasional upgrade regressions in Private (VPC) clusters. On-call currently performs manual checks (instance reboots, taint/untain, terraform refresh/apply) which increases MTTR and risk during upgrades. The Watchtower should reduce manual toil by surfacing a deterministic remediation plan per failure class and executing an automated 'saga' that: (1) validates the problem via synthetic probes and state comparison, (2) attempts non-disruptive fixes (circuit breakers, restarting agent, restarting daemonset), (3) escalates to infrastructure-level remediations using IaC guarded safe-apply (terraform plan dry-run, queued apply with canary), and (4) provides an automated rollback path and human-in-the-loop approval for risky changes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Author a canonical runbook that maps observed symptoms -> probe checklist -> remediation saga steps (with explicit abort/rollback conditions).
- Implement a lightweight orchestrator service (k8s Job + controller or Lambda-style function) that can execute sagas as idempotent steps and emit structured audit logs.
- Provide Terraform modules and automation recipes: drift-detection hooks, safe-apply wrapper (plan + diff gate + snapshot state), and an emergency snapshot/restore play.
- Integrate observability: per-saga traces in Console (events, tokenized costs if applicable), Prometheus metrics for saga attempts/success/failure, and alerting thresholds.
- Add end-to-end tests in staging: fault-injection harness to simulate common failures and assert correct saga behavior and no data-plane disruption.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full multi-tenant authorization for automated applies (we will gate apply to a service account and require approval flow for high-risk changes). Does not replace Dedicated autoscaling policies.

Architecture decisions and trade-offs under consideration:
- Orchestration pattern: long-running controller vs ephemeral step-runner. We prefer ephemeral step-runner for simpler failure semantics and easier replay.
- Use Terraform for infra-level remediations because state is authoritative, but wrap applies in a safe-apply service that enforces plan review and snapshotting.
- Remediation granularity: prefer remote agent restarts and kube-level fixes before any instance reprovision. Reprovisioning is last-resort due to potential work loss.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Security notes: Any automatic apply path must use scoped service principal, strict audit logs, KMS-encrypted state snapshots, and an emergency kill switch. A security review is required before enabling infra applies in prod.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical runbook drafted and reviewed — maps 8 common failure signatures to deterministic remediation sagas
Safe-apply wrapper implemented and documented (terraform plan + gating; snapshot/restore tested)
Orchestrator can execute sagas against staging and report structured events to Console
Fault-injection tests pass in staging: for each failure class, the saga either resolves the issue without reprovision or triggers a documented rollback path
Alerting and runbook links visible in the Console incident view; at-call on-call playbook updated
comments: 2025-01-20 - Leah Chen: Initial spike complete. Prototype step-runner implemented as a Kubernetes Job runner. Key open question: whether to store saga state in etcd (k8s) vs DDB. Leaning towards k8s CRD for discoverability.
2025-01-28 - Ravi Gupta: Reviewed prototype. Request to add a dry-run mode that only emits suggested Terraform plan diffs and does not alter state (for operator validation).
2025-02-02 - Security (Nadia Patel): Security review requested. Must include KMS for state snapshots and role separation for apply path. Added security_review_required flag.

2025-02-06 - SRE (Oliver Reyes): Added observability checklist: saga_histogram, saga_errors, last_success_timestamp, and per-saga tracing IDs tied to Console events. Also proposed using existing alert channel infra-alerts/private-sagas.
2025-02-10 - Leah Chen: Implemented safe-apply prototype and linked PR. Running staging fault-injection now. Next: design canary policy for rolling upgrades using watchtower sagas.
notes: Implementation plan: week 1 write runbook and prototype step-runner; week 2 implement safe-apply and Terraform hooks; week 3 run fault-injection suite in staging and iterate; week 4 security review and gated rollout to limited prod regions. Rollout strategy: enable read-only (dry-run) for 48h, then allow low-risk sagas (agent restarts, kube restarts), then enable infra applies behind human approval. Emergency kill-switch (feature flag) to disable automated applies globally.
